### Voldrak

It seems like every lake in Ustalav of any considerable size has its own legend about a lake monster, but in the case of Lake Laroba, these legends have been fact for as long as anyone can remember. The lake’s denizen, Voldrak, was only rarely sighted in the days before the curse, despite entire expeditions of hopeful monster-watchers spending extensive hours on the lake.

Now, like all other creatures swept up by the Bastardhall Curse, Voldrak has grown worse. The lake monster torments anyone who dares ply the waters for too long. He generally prefers to frighten or maim rather than kill, for this new Voldrak enjoys the knowledge that his horrific legend might spread.

Voldrak is a sleek, plesiosaur-like serpent, with four clawed flippers, deep-red eyes, and a long tail that ends in a single long rudder-like fin. His teeth are long and terrible and protrude over his lips even when his mouth is closed.

Aron Mordimus was orphaned at a young age when his parents, part of a trading expedition heading to Thrushmoor from the far side of Lake Encarthan, were lost at sea during a sudden storm. Infant Aron's survival was a miracle; he was found on the island's shore by a fisherman, crying but swaddled safe and secure in a lifeboat. He grew up as the adopted child of the fisherman, whose own family had perished a few years before during a similar storm, and took his adoptive father's family name, Mordimus, as his own—along with the name his father gave him, Aron. His only clue to his heritage was the sheathed clan dagger the fisherman found in the swaddling. When Aron grew older and began to question why he looked so different from his father, elder Mordimus gave him this dagger and told the story of how he'd come into his life. To his surprise, his adopted son proclaimed him his true father, and while he has long been intrigued by the potential legacy of his clan dagger, he never looked into its history since, to him, he already had a family. After his father passed away of natural causes, Aron did some traveling. During these travels, he became amazed at the variety of inns he encountered, and before long decided innkeeping would be his calling. He eventually settled in the small village of Maiserene and helped to build the inn there, Orm's Rest, and there he still lived when the curse of Bastardhall changed everything. Aron is a hearty-looking, middle-aged dwarf man with black hair and a short beard he wears in a more human style than dwarven. Though he has many interests, he loves nothing more than helping weary travelers relax with mugs of hot cider and the promise of a comfortable bed, and listening to tales of their travels. Once every year, on his “finding day” (the day his father found him adrift in that lifeboat, since he never learned his real birthday), he spends a few hours meditating and regarding his clan dagger, yet has never felt the need to investigate its history more. Ausken knew from a young age that he'd eventually become Maiserene's sheriff. After all, his father was the sheriff, and his grandfather filled that role before him. So confident was he about his destiny that Ausken decided to start early by becoming both a bully and a snitch among the other children of the village. When one bit of bullying resulted in one of his targets nearly drowning, though, his parents (and particularly his father) were shocked and ashamed that their son would resort to such poor behavior. Ausken's father pulled some strings with the nobles and got his son accepted into the castle guard at a young age, hoping the structure and experience would help him learn respect and patience. The following few years proved to be just the thing for Ausken, who learned quickly that “my dad's the sheriff” carried no weight with those inside the castle walls. He came out of this tough-love apprenticeship a better man, yet when his father died suddenly from an accidental fall while attempting to repair a roof in the village, Maiserene wasn't initially welcoming of the new young sheriff. It took years, and the consequences of numerous poor choices, for Ausken to grow into the role and earn the trust and respect of the village... and then the curse came, and everything ended. Ausken is in his early thirties, with a robust mustache, a hearty build, and a stern expression, yet that expression softens when he looks upon the town he spent the last several years of his life defending. When the curse fell, Ausken was the last villager to die, torn apart by monsters even as he fought to defend Maiserene's ruins. Campaign Role Once his soul is restored, Ausken helps the PCs to keep their weapons and armor ready against the increasing dangers they'll face in Bastardhall, and in time he can provide potent magical effects to both. Once he physically manifests, he often spends his time patrolling Maiserene and can serve to guide any remaining explorations of the haunted shore the PCs might have. He can guide them to areas that still need to be investigated and made safe from monstrous influence. Side Quest Soon after the PCs unlock the castle grounds, Ausken approaches to tell them of his time spent serving in the castle guard, likely when they're resting or maintaining their gear. He can sketch out the rough layout of the castle grounds for the PCs and suggests that of all the locations therein, the armory (area **B7**) might be the safest place to hole up and rest if the PCs can't make it back to Maiserene. His expression then grows introspective as he recalls the brief romance he had with another guard in training during that time. It's a relief to him that she left the castle years before the curse fell to seek her destiny as an adventurer in distant lands, but if the PCs can check to see if the romantic pledge they'd carved into wood in the castle's training yard (area **B8**) still exists, he'd appreciate the tiny favor. If they ask where the carving was, his brow furrows and, in frustration, he says he can't recall. If the PCs report back with the information, tears well in his eyes and he thanks them, not only for the report but for the flood of memories they restore to him as they do so. _aon.markdown:
Banijer was born and raised in Maiserene. As a child, he was precocious and willful, spending much of his youth avoiding his lessons and insulting mentor after mentor until, finally, he'd exhausted all goodwill and opportunities for apprenticeship and education in the village. He has the dubious honor of being the first of Maiserene's native locals to serve prison time in the castle's dungeon after he was caught in an ill-advised caper involving smuggling goods. His “partner” in the escapade, the castle's own apothecary, Junth Rundel, betrayed him and sold him out to cover up his own criminal activities. Bitter and disillusioned after being released from prison several months later, Banijer left his home and spent the next several years of his life traveling Ustalav. This time away from home was precisely what Banijer needed to find himself. During these years, he had more than a dozen serious (and not-so-serious) flings with men and women alike, but then he met and fell in love with the woman who would become his wife. When she became pregnant, the two decided to return to Maiserene to live a simpler life than the traveling merchant role Banijer had grown into. Upon his return, Banijer was overcome with waves of guilt and nostalgia as, for the first time, he understood the close-knit support and companionship he'd grown up among but had never appreciated. Over the next 10 years, Banijer did his best to atone for his rebellious youth. His family grew, and he took over the duties of his family's farm on the east shore of the isle. When the first man he'd apprenticed to died of old age, Banijer was shocked to learn the man had left him the village trading post in his will. Since that day, up until the night of the curse, Banijer spent every day working to bolster the town's prosperity while seeing to it his children were raised with an appreciation for their home. Banijer is a middle-aged human man with salt and pepper hair, a wiry frame, and a quirky style that heavily features mismatched colors. He's eager to laugh and joke, but when he's alone, his thoughts turn morose, and his expression takes on a haunted visage. On the night of the curse, Banijer raced back to the farmhouse where his family was hiding, then sacrificed himself in a desperate attempt to lure the monsters away from the home. Yet his death was only the start of his agony. His ultimate fate was perhaps the most tragic of all six of the town's leaders, as Charg seized upon his childhood disdain for local life and forced him to watch from inside the monster the curse had turned him into as it slaughtered his family. Banijer remembers this with shame and a quiet fury but never speaks of it aloud. Campaign RoleBanijer's role in the campaign is simple—as the local trader, his influence and presence gives the PCs someone they can sell items to and purchase items from. He can also offer spellcasting services for standard prices. He's always eager to talk about any treasures the PCs find while exploring, and once both he and Aron Mordimus physically manifest, the two swiftly rekindle their old friendship. This friendship eventually blossoms into a full-fledged romance after Aron helps Banijer come to terms with the cruelty he endured when his family perished. As he gives them the map, he pauses, then notes that as he tried to evade capture that fateful night, he lost the silver sickle his father had given him. At the time, he didn't really care about it, but now he misses the sickle; he tells the PCs that if they find themselves down in the dungeon, “that two-faced Junth” likely found it and claimed it as his own. creature.flavor:
### Banijer Greely

Banijer was born and raised in Maiserene. As a child, he was precocious and willful, spending much of his youth avoiding his lessons and insulting mentor after mentor until, finally, he'd exhausted all goodwill and opportunities for apprenticeship and education in the village. He has the dubious honor of being the first of Maiserene's native locals to serve prison time in the castle's dungeon after he was caught in an ill-advised caper involving smuggling goods. His “partner” in the escapade, the castle's own apothecary, Junth Rundel, betrayed him and sold him out to cover up his own criminal activities. Bitter and disillusioned after being released from prison several months later, Banijer left his home and spent the next several years of his life traveling Ustalav.

This time away from home was precisely what Banijer needed to find himself. During these years, he had more than a dozen serious (and not-so-serious) flings with men and women alike, but then he met and fell in love with the woman who would become his wife. When she became pregnant, the two decided to return to Maiserene to live a simpler life than the traveling merchant role Banijer had grown into. Upon his return, Banijer was overcome with waves of guilt and nostalgia as, for the first time, he understood the close-knit support and companionship he'd grown up among but had never appreciated.

Over the next 10 years, Banijer did his best to atone for his rebellious youth. His family grew, and he took over the duties of his family's farm on the east shore of the isle. When the first man he'd apprenticed to died of old age, Banijer was shocked to learn the man had left him the village trading post in his will. Since that day, up until the night of the curse, Banijer spent every day working to bolster the town's prosperity while seeing to it his children were raised with an appreciation for their home.

Banijer is a middle-aged human man with salt and pepper hair, a wiry frame, and a quirky style that heavily features mismatched colors. He's eager to laugh and joke, but when he's alone, his thoughts turn morose, and his expression takes on a haunted visage. On the night of the curse, Banijer raced back to the farmhouse where his family was hiding, then sacrificed himself in a desperate attempt to lure the monsters away from the home. Yet his death was only the start of his agony. His ultimate fate was perhaps the most tragic of all six of the town's leaders, as Charg seized upon his childhood disdain for local life and forced him to watch from inside the monster the curse had turned him into as it slaughtered his family. Banijer remembers this with shame and a quiet fury but never speaks of it aloud.

Ilana Greenbough was born far from Ustalav, in a Varisian caravan traveling the routes along Varisia's Lost Cost. This particular caravan had long integrated halflings into their traveling families, and their skills at artistry and on-the-road repair work came naturally to her as she grew older and learned the ways and complications of traveling folk. Some time after reaching adulthood, tragedy struck when the caravan was ambushed by ogres—Ilana was the sole survivor. Eager to put distance between a land that now only brought back memories of sadness, she traveled east. It was chance that saw her eventually settle in Maiserene, a small town that charmed her with its mix of beautiful landscapes and stunning architecture. Ilana is a vibrant halfling woman whose hairstyle changes often to match her daily whims. (Not quite as frequently as a gnome's would, but she's always trying out new things.) Traditional Varisian tattoos adorn her shoulders, arms, and back. She's rarely seen without her leather toolbelt and a backpack filled with painting supplies—as she's eager to point out, “You never know when inspiration might come knocking, or when that knocking might actually be something that needs a quick fix!” When the curse struck Castle Arudora, Ilana was a key element in planning how to destroy the Laroba Bridge with fire—Maiserene's desperate attempt to contain the horrors after it became apparent the village was doomed. Her solution, jury-rigged trebuchet-like devices meant to fling bottles of flammable liquid, proved to be so effective that the bridge's destruction was swift. Unfortunately, she didn't live long after that realization; one of the unleashed monsters snatched her up and dropped her into the very fires she'd helped to ignite. Campaign Role Once she returns to her bench in Maiserene's workshop, Ilana helps to ensure the site remains well-stocked for the PCs' use and opens the location up for characters to help produce materials so that they can Earn Income, repair items, or even craft their own items. At your discretion, she could even craft items for the PCs, giving them one other way to shop for items beyond the trading post. Side Quest Once the PCs unlock the castle grounds, Ilana approaches them with a concern of hers. She tells them about an amazing art gallery in the reception halls she would visit as often as possible, and once that area unlocks, she urges the PCs to check whether it and the pieces on display within survived, or if it's still being curated by someone (or something). More to the point, though, on the day before the curse struck, Ilana had been visiting the gallery to speak about potentially having one of her own paintings—a landscape of Castle Arudora—displayed in the gallery. She left her painting there with the gallery's curator, Ilves Mondain, and while she doesn't expect it to have survived all this time, if the PCs could look for it in the gallery, in Ilves' office, or anywhere else, she would be grateful. _aon.markdown:
Shirail's parents impressed the importance of faith upon her from a young age, but they heavily tempered those lessons with an even greater focus on tolerance and acceptance. Her father, a priest of Shelyn, and her mother, a priestess of Pharasma, showed her the ways two very different beliefs could support each other and expand on the core tenets of each religion, so that when she came of age and became an adventurer, she had little difficulty finding a place among such an eclectic group. Once she began adventuring, Shirail's presence and temperament helped to bolster her group's teamwork and morale. Things were going fine, at least, until a tragic expedition into a haunted swamp in Versex left only Shirail alive among her group. Unable to singlehandedly transport the bodies of her companions back home to be properly buried according to their cultures and beliefs, Shirail cremated the three in a pyre she built there in the swamp. She stayed until the pyre was cool, then gathered their ashes before fleeing back home. Her excitement of the adventuring lifestyle waned after that, and when an opportunity arrived to serve as the caretaker and priestess for a new church of Pharasma, it was easy for her to choose to join the villagers of Maiserene. She was ready to stay put and really serve a community. Shirail appears as a beautiful elf woman whose expression always carries at least a hint of somber introspection, as if she carries unpleasant memories that are never far from her mind. When the curse struck the castle and the surrounding village, Shirail perished in the defense of the church, grimly standing against undead animated from the remains of her one-time flock until the forces of the curse overwhelmed her. Campaign Role Shirail's power over life and death has grown stronger now that she's experienced death herself, and her support can help to restore PCs who have perished. She can also perform spellcasting services for the PCs for the standard prices, and can eventually teach certain formulas for a few rituals to the PCs as well. Side Quest Shirail kept her companions' ashes with her for a time, but after she accepted a post at Maiserene and struck up a friendship with the castle's priestess of Pharasma, she secured permission to have her friends' ashes interred in urns in the castle crypt. On the night of the curse, as she defended her church, she was attacked and mortally wounded by distorted, ghostly mockeries of her adventuring companions' ghosts. As she lay dying, she watched the three ghosts mock and deride her before retreating upward to the old temple of Pharasma in the southwestern portion of Castle Arudora above. Shirail had heard rumors in the months leading up to the night of the curse that an Arudora had been at work restoring the temple—but not to the worship of Pharasma. ### Shirail Animender

Shirail's parents impressed the importance of faith upon her from a young age, but they heavily tempered those lessons with an even greater focus on tolerance and acceptance. Her father, a priest of Shelyn, and her mother, a priestess of Pharasma, showed her the ways two very different beliefs could support each other and expand on the core tenets of each religion, so that when she came of age and became an adventurer, she had little difficulty finding a place among such an eclectic group.

Once she began adventuring, Shirail's presence and temperament helped to bolster her group's teamwork and morale. Things were going fine, at least, until a tragic expedition into a haunted swamp in Versex left only Shirail alive among her group. Unable to singlehandedly transport the bodies of her companions back home to be properly buried according to their cultures and beliefs, Shirail cremated the three in a pyre she built there in the swamp. She stayed until the pyre was cool, then gathered their ashes before fleeing back home.

Her excitement of the adventuring lifestyle waned after that, and when an opportunity arrived to serve as the caretaker and priestess for a new church of Pharasma, it was easy for her to choose to join the villagers of Maiserene. She was ready to stay put and really serve a community. Shirail appears as a beautiful elf woman whose expression always carries at least a hint of somber introspection, as if she carries unpleasant memories that are never far from her mind. When the curse struck the castle and the surrounding village, Shirail perished in the defense of the church, grimly standing against undead animated from the remains of her one-time flock until the forces of the curse overwhelmed her.
